public_rationale: The Almanac's March 2026 report describes rising valuations at leading tech companies and $92 billion in venture funding in Silicon Valley and San Francisco during 2025 [e1]. It reports a net Silicon Valley employment decline of about 13,100 jobs from mid-2024 to mid-2025 [e1]. This evidence establishes neither an industry-wide end to hyper-growth nor a valuation decline causing tens of thousands of layoffs and an unprecedented prolonged regional depression [e1]. It therefore neither establishes the predicted causal sequence nor decisively rules it out [e1].
limitations: The evidence is secondary reporting on a regional index; the underlying report was not available for verification.
The 13,100-job decline is net employment change from mid-2024 to mid-2025, not a count of gross layoffs [e1].
The report does not establish the proposed causal connections or a regional downturn exceeding previous downturns in severity and duration [e1].
The claim specifies no deadline or measurement rules for hyper-growth, a massive valuation reckoning, or an unprecedented prolonged depression.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The end of tech hyper-growth will cause a massive valuation reckoning, tens of thousands of layoffs, and an unprecedented prolonged depression in Silicon Valley.

statement.excerpt: The ramifications of the end of hyper-growth mean a massive reckoning for the valuations of tech companies, which will lead to tens of thousands of layoffs and a prolonged depression in Silicon Valley, the likes of which we've never seen.
statement.document_title: The Phony Comforts of AI Optimism

from_speaker: a massive reckoning for the valuations of tech companies
a prolonged depression in Silicon Valley
the likes of which we've never seen
our_interpretation: This is a conditional prediction of a causal sequence, with no deadline.

The ordinary reading requires a broad end to exceptional tech-industry growth, followed by a substantial valuation decline that causes at least 20,000 layoffs and an exceptionally severe, sustained regional downturn.
A slowdown at selected companies or layoffs alone would not establish the antecedent or the complete prediction.
The speaker supplies no growth measure, valuation threshold, regional boundary, duration or historical comparison method. I do not invent numerical thresholds for those terms.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the end of industry-wide hyper-growth and the subsequent causal sequence: a major valuation correction, tens of thousands of resulting layoffs, and a sustained Silicon Valley contraction exceeding previous regional downturns in severity and duration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent is established, a completed economic episode would need to decisively rule out the predicted sequence. Continued growth or the absence of a depression by an evaluator-selected date does not falsify this undated forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Consistent industry growth and valuation data, dated layoff records, regional employment and output data, and historical comparisons establishing a completed episode after industry-wide hyper-growth ended. Support requires every predicted consequence and the causal connections.
